description: This nested donut chart illustrates the distribution of responses across two levels of ambiguity, represented by an outer and an inner ring. The chart contains a total of six slices, with three categories displayed in each ring. Two legends on the right side of the figure define the color-coded categories for each level. The outer ring, corresponding to the top legend labeled "Ambiguity 1 (Outer)," consists of a red slice representing "Deceived" at 67.6%, a yellow slice for "Partially" at 23.5%, and a dark green slice for "Not Deceived" at 8.8%. The inner ring, corresponding to the bottom legend labeled "Ambiguity 2 (Inner)," includes a red slice for "Deceived" at 57.9%, a yellow slice for "Partially" at 31.6%, and a light green slice for "Not Deceived" at 10.5%. Percentage labels are positioned directly inside their respective slices in bold text. None of the segments are visually emphasized, exploded, or offset. In both the inner and outer rings, the slices appear to be ordered by descending size.
caption_used: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of responses across two levels of ambiguity, labeled as Ambiguity 1 (Outer) and Ambiguity 2 (Inner). For Ambiguity 1, the majority of responses fall under 'Deceived' at approximately 70%, followed by 'Partially' at 20%, and 'Not Deceived' at 10%. For Ambiguity 2, the 'Deceived' category shows a significant decline to 50%, while 'Partially' increases to 40%, and 'Not Deceived' remains stable at 10%. The chart highlights a notable shift in responses between the two levels of ambiguity, with a marked increase in partial deception and a decrease in full deception.
